title: A Simple, Effective Homework Plan For Teachers: Part 2
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Concluding a two-part series, Linsin lays out the final four strategies of his homework plan. He advises against collecting homework at all, since students rarely benefit from delayed grading, and instead recommends a 'partner check' where students pair up to cross-check answers and resolve discrepancies before the next lesson. Completed homework should then be thrown away—a symbolic act, sometimes turned into a fun basketball-style toss into a wastebasket—underscoring that its only purpose was practice. Students who arrive without finished homework, and who don't complete it during partner check, must do it at home that night in addition to the next day's assignment, which he calls 'doubling.' Linsin closes by challenging readers to try the eight-strategy plan and offering a free book to anyone whose classroom doesn't improve as a result.
points: Don't collect homework for grading; instead have students pair up for a 'partner check' to cross-verify answers before the next lesson.
Throw completed homework away once it has served its purpose as practice, optionally turning disposal into a fun class activity.
Students who cannot participate in partner check because their homework is incomplete must finish it immediately, without joining the activity.
Use a 'doubling' consequence: incomplete homework must be finished at home that night in addition to the next day's regular assignment.
The plan is framed as a challenge, with Linsin offering a free book to any teacher who tries it and doesn't see improved results.
quotes: Collecting homework is a waste of time. Here’s why: Upon return, nearly all students will stuff it in their desk or backpack and not give it another thought.
Instead of collecting it, have your students pair up and cross check their answers. Why? Because it adds ownership, motivation, and accountability to homework.
It’s done. You squeezed all the learning you needed from it. Now it’s time to throw the homework away. There is no reason to keep it.
Ask your students to crumble up their homework, and on your signal, shoot it at the basket.
Any student who comes to school without homework completed, and doesn’t get it finished during partner check, must do it at home that evening along with the homework assigned for the day.
